narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which estimated a 58% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a figure just above the threshold that led to your application being denied. While this is not an overwhelming margin, it reflects a combination of factors in your financial profile that, taken together, raised enough concern to result in a rejection.

To help you understand this decision, it is useful to think about "what if" scenarios — alternative versions of your profile that would have led to an approval. These scenarios identify the smallest changes to your situation that would flip the outcome from denied to approved, giving you a concrete roadmap for what matters most to the system.

In your case, the analysis generated one such scenario, and it points to a single, decisive factor: the status of your checking account. Currently, your checking account shows a negative balance, meaning it is overdrawn. The one scenario that would result in approval requires only this one change — moving your checking account to a healthy standing, specifically to a status of having no checking account or a positive balance. Every other aspect of your profile — the loan amount of 3,394 DM, the 42-month duration, your credit history, your savings, your employment situation, and all other factors — remained exactly the same in the alternative scenario. This tells us that the checking account status is, by far, the most critical issue flagged by the system.

To put this in context, among applicants who were approved, about half had no checking account at all, roughly 23% had a balance between 0 and 200 DM, and only about 20% were in a negative balance situation like yours. Being overdrawn signals financial instability to the model, and in your case, it appears to be the tipping point. It is worth noting that several other aspects of your profile are already working against you in combination — your loan duration of 42 months is more than double the average of 19 months seen among approved applicants, your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the approved average of roughly 3%, and being currently unemployed places you in a very small group among approved borrowers. Your purpose of the loan — home repairs — is also among the least common reasons for approved loans, representing under 2% of approvals.

The most actionable step you can take is to resolve the negative balance in your checking account before reapplying. If you are able to bring your account into good standing, the model suggests this alone could be sufficient to change the outcome. Additionally, while the counterfactual did not require it, reducing the loan duration or the requested amount could further strengthen your application given how far those figures currently sit above typical approved profiles.
